uncited: This family encompasses rendering systems that offload volume rendering computations to parallel hardware (GPUs, multi-core CPUs) or execute entirely within web browsers using WebGL/WebGPU.
It addresses the computational intensity of volume rendering by leveraging massive parallelism for tasks like ray casting, splatting, and data sorting.

It is distinguished from [Voxel engines and games](47-voxel-engines-and-games.md) by its focus on general-purpose visualization rather than game engine integration, and from [Film and production rendering](48-film-and-production-rendering.md) by its emphasis on real-time or near-real-time interactivity and web compatibility.
The core mechanism involves mapping volumetric data processing onto parallel execution units.
**Depth Sorting**: For alpha-blended rendering (e.g., splatting), fragments or splats must be sorted by depth.
Designed to work without a dedicated rendering backend and relies only on a file server.
